title: Sterkfontein Caves, Cradle of Humankind
summary: Sterkfontein is a group of limestone caves in Gauteng, South Africa, within UNESCO's Fossil Hominid Sites of South Africa. Its deposits run from about 3.67 million to about 250,000 years ago and have yielded over 800 fossils from four hominin species, including the skull nicknamed Mrs Ples and the skeleton called Little Foot.

uncertainty.note: Converted as year = 1950 minus age. Popular Archaeology gives deposits from about 3.67 million to about 250,000 years ago; Mrs Ples 2.05-2.01 Ma and Little Foot 3.67 Ma (most recent estimate, classification debated).

as_recorded.value: Deposits span from about 3.67 million years ago to about 250,000 years ago

where.modern_name: Sterkfontein Caves, near Krugersdorp, Gauteng, South Africa
where.historical_name: Sterkfontein Valley dolomite caves; no polities exist at this date

paleo.plate_model: MERDITH2021 (Merdith et al. 2021, Earth-Science Reviews 214:103477) via GPlates Web Service
paleo.note: Reconstruction to 3.67 Ma moves the point about 210 km south.

importance.justification: Richest source of Australopithecus africanus fossils and home of Little Foot, a core site of the Cradle of Humankind.
